applicable_when: ALLOW_TF32=False forces tl.dot to use scalar FP32 FFMA instead of Tensor Cores. This causes catastrophic register pressure (255 registers/thread — the hardware maximum), which: (1) limits occupancy to 12.5% (only 2 blocks/SM), (2) forces the compiler to spill registers to local memory causing the 83.31% speedup-potential uncoalesced local load/store pattern, and (3) causes 8-way shared memory bank conflicts from spill/reload traffic. Enabling TF32 (allow_tf32=True) routes tl.dot through Tensor Core MMA instructions, which are handled by dedicated hardware units — dramatically reducing register pressure, eliminating local memory spills, and unlocking ~14.7x higher peak throughput (989 vs 67 TFLOPS). M=256, N=8192, K=16384 is a large GEMM where TF32 precision is appropriate.
